title: TOC double-escapes `<`, `>` and `&` from code spans in headers and puts entity names in the ids
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`. When a header contains inline code with HTML special characters, the table of contents shows the escaped entities literally and the generated id is built from the entity names. ``` md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['markdown.extensions.toc']) md.convert('[TOC]\n\n# ``') ``` Expected: ```
\n
    \n
  • <test>
    • \n
\n
\n

<test>

``` Actual: ```
\n
    \n
  • <test>
    • \n
\n
\n

<test>

``` So a reader sees `<test>` in the TOC, and the anchor is `#lttestgt`. Same with ``# Use `a & b` ``: the TOC link reads `Use a & b` and the id is `use-a-amp-b` instead of `use-a-b`. Characters inside a code span in a header should be treated as the characters they are, both for the TOC text (escaped exactly once) and for the slug, just like the same characters outside code.
acceptance: The reported header renders with TOC text `<test>` and id `test`
Code spans containing `&`, `<` or `>` in headers are escaped once in the TOC and do not leak entity names into ids
